title: Portal API refusal
description: The one shape the portal's API refuses with (portal plan P1.0, P1.1). Every route answers it, so it is the one shape here that is not mounted by name: the SPA branches on `code` and shows `message`, and a route that answered a sentence of its own would put the frontend's behaviour in wording that changes. Every object in this folder is closed, because the Go reader (ee/keyservice/wire_*.go, decodeWire) refuses an unknown field: a body or an answer that carried one is a schema and a reader that disagree, and the fixture tests in ee/keyservice/wire_test.go are what catch it.

refusal.description: A refusal: the machine's name for what went wrong and a sentence for the person. It never carries the request, an address or a token — a refusal is read by whoever sent the request and by logs, and neither is a place for the body someone sent.

code.description: The stable, machine-readable name of the refusal, in lower snake case. The SPA switches on it, so renaming one is changing a wire format (CLAUDE.md: a field never changes meaning).

message.description: One sentence for the person. It may quote what the caller sent — an address, a project id, an organisation's name — so the SPA renders it as text and never as markup.
